The denominator is $-2-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-2+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-2+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5+2\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}} & =\frac{5+2\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-2+3\text{i}}{-2+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{(5+2\text{i})(-2+3\text{i})}{(-2)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10+15\text{i}-4\text{i}+6{\text{i}}^{2}}{4-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{-10+11\text{i}+6(-1)}{13} \\  & =\frac{-16+11\text{i}}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-16+11\text{i}}{13}=(-\frac{16}{13})+(\frac{11}{13})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
